title: Polar pattern hashing — pattern, not number
summary: dev9 adds curve-relative polar pattern hashing: source minimum is the centre, amplitude becomes normalized radius, sample position becomes angular progress, and radius/slope/curvature differences are ordered by significance so one major shape disagreement dominates many small ones.
authority: Executable dev9 source/tests and the self-generating polar SVG demo are authoritative. Pattern hashing complements, rather than replaces, dev8 scalar close-neighbour hashing.
invariants: Pattern identity is about relative curve geometry, not absolute source offset, amplitude or source sample count.
The canonical reference representation is a circular polar grid: source minimum maps to radius 0, source maximum to radius 1, and source samples are resampled onto a fixed angular grid.
Original minimum, maximum, sample count and canonical rotation remain evidence even when they do not define pattern identity.
The signature retains quantized radius, first circular difference and second circular difference; curvature policy may carry greater significance than residual radius.
Pattern distance is lexicographic over weighted local differences sorted largest-first. The largest structural disagreement dominates collections of smaller disagreements.
Rotation invariance is explicit policy; reversal invariance is opt-in because traversal direction can carry domain meaning.
MLPatternIndex is a driveable historical object. Alternative pattern schemas or invariance policies should be branched and compared rather than overwriting the only fitted index.
A pattern match is candidate evidence, not a causal or cryptanalytic conclusion.
procedure: Create MLPatternHashPolicy with angular resolution, radial quantization and radius/slope/curvature significance weights.
Use MLPatternHashSchema to encode a source curve; inspect polarPoints when visual explanation matters.
Use rotationInvariant only when the starting phase/index is not semantic; enable reversalInvariant only when forward/backward traversal are genuinely equivalent.
Build MLPatternCorpus and MLPatternIndex for recognition over variable-length curves with stable sample ids.
Compare matches using MLPatternHashDifference dominantDelta and the full significance-ordered rank, not opaque integer subtraction.
Run examples/pattern_hash_polar_demo.rex and inspect its generated SVG before deploying the technique to a new domain.
For cryptanalytic, audio, camera or telemetry work, treat recurrence as a lead for further domain analysis, never as standalone proof.
